name: Hassium

discovery.discoverer: Peter Armbruster & Gottfried Münzenberg, GSI Darmstadt

occurrence: Does not occur naturally; produced only via particle accelerator fusion, atom by atom.
majorUses: No practical applications — pure superheavy-element research
safetyNotes: Intensely radioactive; observed only as individual atoms with half-lives of a fraction of a second to roughly ten seconds.
notableCharacteristics: Named after Hesse, the German state where the GSI Helmholtz Centre laboratory that discovered it is located.
whyHere: Predicted to sit in Group 8 directly below osmium, hassium is expected to be even denser than osmium if enough of it could ever be gathered, though so far chemists have only confirmed traces of osmium-like reactivity from single-atom experiments.
didYouKnow: If enough hassium could somehow be collected in bulk, theoretical predictions suggest it could be the densest element in the entire periodic table, even denser than osmium — though nobody has ever made more than a few atoms at once to test this.
genZNote: Predicted to be the densest element ever, if we could actually make more than a few atoms of it at a time. Forever a hypothetical heavyweight champion.
